title: Pelicans agree to trade Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy to Grizzlies: Sources
content:
The New Orleans Pelicans agreed to trade Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson on Tuesday, league sources confirmed to The Athletic.

ESPN was first to report the news.

The Pelicans move on from two of their former draft picks and future draft capital to free up $5.7 million in wiggle room below the first apron and complete their anticipated signing of former Clippers guard Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal that the two sides agreed upon a few weeks ago. New Orleans will also generate a $7 million trade exception by moving Hawkins.

New Orleans will likely waive Gibson and his non-guaranteed $3.8 million salary as part of the process, per a team source who spoke on the condition of anonymity because the deal was not complete. Johnson will remain with the Pels and get a chance to show what he can do in training camp, per a team source.

Memphis continues its rebuild by adding two more young prospects on the perimeter and draft compensation.

Hawkins, 24, was selected No. 14 overall by New Orleans in the 2023 NBA Draft and showed some potential early in his career as a sharpshooter before mostly falling out of the rotation last season. In three seasons with the Pels, he averaged 8 points and 2.3 rebounds while shooting 37.4 percent from the field and 34.8 percent from 3-point distance.

Peavy, 25, was taken with the No. 40 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft by New Orleans and quickly became a fan favorite because of his defensive tenacity as an on-ball stopper. During his rookie season, he averaged 4.3 points and 1.9 rebounds.

— John Hollinger contributed to this story
